pr_title: sysext: Fix issues with merged hierarchy mode
pr_body:
There seems to be a regression, where merged hierarchy ends up having `0700` permissions, which breaks boot on Flatcar. No binary under `/usr` can be executed - we are getting `permission denied` errors.

The PR:
- fixes some small error reporting issues,
- makes sysext to ensure that the merged hierarchy has the same mode as the underlying hierarchy
- makes sysext to require that the preexisting mutable directory has the same mode as the underlying hierarchy
- adds tests
- makes the tests to run also on `/` (so without the `--root` flag)
- checks for used extensions before potentially creating the mutable directory when in `--mutable=yes` mode
  - so we will skip creating the directory if we there are no extensions for the hierarchy at all thus no overlay will be created
- addresses post-merge review issues from https://github.com/systemd/systemd/pull/31801#pullrequestreview-1993682430
- closes #32217
pr_comments: Currently building a Flatcar image with those patches to see if they fix the booting problem. If they do, I'll mark this PR as ready for review.

The failures in CI seem to be unrelated and of the same nature - not able to install same debian test dependencies.

Also, the PR seems to have a missing `sysext` label.
(FYI should be merged before the next release)

The issue this PR fixes was originally reported in https://github.com/systemd/systemd/pull/31000#issuecomment-1948455247 and I forgot to check it again before the PR got merged.
I've tested this PR here for the read-only (default) merge case and it now works, but for the `--mutable=yes` case I get this new error:
```
Assertion 'root' failed at src/sysext/sysext.c:780, function mutable_directory_mode_matches_hierarchy(). Aborting.
```

One more small issue I ran into is that the `ephemeral-import` only works after `mkdir -p /var/lib/extensions.mutable/opt` but not when the folder doesn't exist - I think because the test sysext only ships `/usr` and thus there is no lowerdir for `/opt`. But ideally this would still work because in the end no overlay mount for `/opt` is set up even after creating `/var/lib/extensions.mutable/opt`.
```
# systemd-sysext refresh --mutable=ephemeral-import
Using extensions 'test'.
Unmerged '/usr'.
Not importing mutable directory for hierarchy /opt as a lower dir, because it points to the hierarchy itself
Failed to merge hierarchies
```

Updated.

While working on updating the tests to run also on `/` I noticed one thing (it's marked as TODO in three or so places in the test script) - if I have only one extension and it puts stuff into `/opt/` only, then using `--mutable=yes` will cause `/usr/` to also become mutable, because the extensions need to contain `/usr/lib/extension-release.d/extension-release.${name}` to be even considered as an extension - this means that extension is also "extending" `/usr/` thus making it mutable too.

I'm not sure if anything should be done with it, but maybe we could say that if the extension has only `/usr/lib/extension-release.d/extension-release.${name}` then `/usr/` will be overlaid, but as readonly in such case. In order to have it mutable too, create some other dummy file under `/usr/`. This maybe would need some more changes in uapi extensions draft to allow implementations to decide to create a read-only overlay in certain situations.
Thanks for the fixes, I've retested it and now it works with `--mutable=yes` and `ephemeral-import` even without creating the `opt` subdir.

> I'm not sure if anything should be done with it, but maybe we could say that if the extension has only `/usr/lib/extension-release.d/extension-release.${name}` then `/usr/` will be overlaid, but as readonly in such case. In order to have it mutable too, create some other dummy file under `/usr/`. This maybe would need some more changes in uapi extensions draft to allow implementations to decide to create a read-only overlay in certain situations.

Having different behavior based on the contents of extensions is something I would want to avoid because it leads to surprising behavior. Ideally we would even have a way of always setting up the mountpoint to further align the behavior. Whether `/usr`and `/opt` become mutable together or separate is something I would expect to be a new flag (and yes, I'm still convinced about the need for having a config file because that's the only sane way we can set up the overlay from the initrd the same way the final system would do, because otherwise one would have to parse the drop-in units for the env vars…).
